content: If you've ever opened the cabinet under your kitchen or bathroom sink and felt a wave of overwhelm wash over you, trust me - you are absolutely not alone. That dark, awkward space is one of the most neglected spots in any home, but it also has enormous potential. With the right **under sink organization ideas**, you can turn that chaotic jumble of cleaning supplies, spare soap bottles, and mystery items into a streamlined, easy-to-use storage zone that works hard for your daily routine. In 2026, smart home organization is all about using every single inch wisely, and the space under your sink deserves the same attention as the rest of your home.
![Under sink organization ideas with pull-out drawers, clear bins, and tension rod for spray bottles in a modern kitchen](/images/blog/under-sink-organization-ideas-hero.webp)
## Why Under Sink Organization Ideas Matter More Than You Think

The under-sink cabinet is one of the most frequently accessed spots in your kitchen and bathroom, yet it tends to collect clutter faster than almost anywhere else in the house. Think about it: cleaning products, extra paper towels, trash bags, sponges, extra toiletries, drain cleaner, and more all get stuffed under there with little rhyme or reason. Without a proper system, you end up digging through everything every time you need something simple.

According to [The Spruce](https://www.thespruce.com), under-sink cabinets are among the top five most disorganized areas in American homes, largely because of their irregular shape, the pipe running through the center, and the lack of built-in shelving. But the good news? The right products and a clear strategy can completely change that.
A well-organized under-sink cabinet means:
• **Faster access** to cleaning supplies when you need them
• **Fewer duplicate purchases** because you can actually see what you own
• **Better hygiene** since surfaces stay dry and easy to wipe down
• **Safer storage** for any products that need to be kept away from children
• **A calmer home** because less clutter equals less mental noise

If you're already working on organizing other parts of your home, check out our guide on [30+ best kitchen cabinet organization ideas](/blog/kitchen-cabinet-organization-ideas) and [30+ best bathroom storage ideas](/blog/bathroom-storage-ideas) for even more inspiration.
## Step 1: Start with a Complete Cleanout
Before you can implement any under sink organization ideas, you need a blank canvas. Pull everything out from under the sink completely. Yes, everything.
Once it's all out, sort items into four groups:
1. **Keep** - Products you actively use and are not expired
2. **Toss** - Empty bottles, expired products, or anything you haven't touched in over a year
3. **Relocate** - Items that don't belong under the sink at all
4. **Donate** - Unopened, usable products you simply don't need

While the cabinet is empty, take a moment to wipe down the interior with an all-purpose cleaner. Let it dry completely. If you notice any moisture or mildew, address it before putting anything back. A dry, clean cabinet is the foundation of a long-lasting organization system.

Next, measure your cabinet dimensions. Note the interior width, depth, and height - and importantly, measure around the pipes so you know exactly what space you're working with. These measurements will guide every product you purchase.

## The Best Under Sink Organization Ideas for Your Kitchen

The kitchen sink cabinet faces a unique set of challenges: a large drain pipe in the middle, often a garbage disposal unit, and the need to store bulky cleaning supplies. Here are the most effective under sink organization ideas specifically for kitchen cabinets.
![Stackable clear bins and two-tier pull-out organizer for under sink kitchen cabinet storage](/images/blog/under-sink-organization-ideas-section-1.webp)
### 1. Use a Two-Tier Pull-Out Organizer

A pull-out shelf organizer is one of the best investments you can make for your kitchen under-sink cabinet. These slide out smoothly so you can easily reach items at the very back without contorting your arm into an awkward angle. Look for U-shaped designs that accommodate your drain pipe.
### 2. Install a Tension Rod for Spray Bottles

This is one of the most talked-about under sink organization ideas on platforms like [Pinterest](https://www.pinterest.com) - and for good reason. A simple tension rod installed horizontally across the cabinet lets you hang spray bottle triggers from it, freeing up the entire floor of the cabinet for other storage. It costs very little and takes about 30 seconds to install.
### 3. Add a Stackable Shelf Riser

A small shelf riser placed to one side of the pipe creates an instant second level of storage, effectively doubling your usable space. Use the upper level for lighter items like sponges, dish soap, or gloves, and the lower level for heavier items.
### 4. Use Clear Stackable Bins

Clear bins let you see exactly what's inside without pulling everything out. Group like items together - one bin for dish cleaning supplies, one for trash bags, one for rubber gloves. Label the front of each bin for even faster access.
### 5. Add a Small Lazy Susan

A lazy susan turntable is perfect for storing smaller items like dish soap, sponges, or small cleaning bottles. Spin it to access items in the back without reaching - a total game changer in tight cabinet spaces.
### 6. Mount a Door-Mounted Organizer

The inside of your cabinet door is prime real estate you're probably not using. A door-mounted rack or over-the-door organizer can hold sponges, scrubbers, small bottles, or even a trash bag dispenser. Just make sure it doesn't interfere with the cabinet's closing.
### 7. Use a Caddy for Everyday Cleaning Supplies

A portable cleaning caddy - the kind you can carry from room to room - keeps your most-used cleaning products grouped together and easy to grab. This is especially useful if you clean multiple areas of your home with the same products.
### 8. Install a Small Trash Can or Recycling Bin
If space allows, tucking a slim trash can or a small recycling bin under the kitchen sink is a smart use of that corner space and keeps countertops cleaner.

## Under Sink Organization Ideas for the Bathroom

The bathroom under-sink cabinet has its own set of quirks - it's usually smaller than the kitchen version and tends to store a wide variety of items from toiletries to hair tools to medicine. Here's how to bring order to the chaos.
![Under bathroom sink organization with tension rod, lazy susan, baskets, and bamboo shelf riser](/images/blog/under-sink-organization-ideas-section-2.webp)
### 1. Use Baskets or Bins Grouped by Category

Divide your bathroom under-sink items into categories: hair care, skincare, first aid, feminine hygiene, cleaning, and so on. Assign one basket or bin per category. Wicker baskets add warmth and texture while keeping everything corralled. Clear acrylic bins work great if you prefer a modern, spa-like aesthetic.
### 2. Try a Stackable Organizer with Drawers

Small stackable drawer units are incredibly versatile for bathroom under-sink storage. They fit beside the pipe and let you stack multiple levels of storage vertically, making the most of the cabinet's height.
### 3. Use a Bamboo Shelf Riser

Similar to the kitchen approach, a bamboo shelf riser elevates one set of products and creates a second storage tier. Bamboo is a popular choice for bathrooms because it's moisture-resistant and brings a natural, calming aesthetic.
### 4. Hang a Lazy Susan for Skincare and Toiletries
A compact lazy susan is perfect for storing skincare bottles, lotions, and small toiletries under the bathroom sink. Spin it to access everything without rearranging the whole cabinet.
### 5. Add a Hair Tool Holder

Hair dryers, flat irons, and curling wands can take up a lot of space and create a mess of tangled cords. A heat-resistant hair tool holder that mounts to the cabinet wall or sits on the floor is a simple but transformative addition.
### 6. Use Stackable Organizers for Toiletry Backstock
If you buy toiletries in bulk (thank you, membership warehouse stores), keep backstock neatly stacked in a labeled bin at the back of the cabinet so you always know when you're running low.
### 7. Add a Small Trash Bin

A slim, narrow trash bin tucked under the bathroom sink keeps waste out of sight and reduces counter clutter. Many people find this is one of the simplest under sink organization ideas with one of the biggest everyday payoffs.
### 8. Hang an Adhesive Organizer on the Door

Adhesive door organizers are perfect for bathrooms where drilling isn't an option. They hold small items like cotton balls, hair ties, tweezers, and nail clippers - things that always seem to float around without a home.

> **Pro tip from Real Simple:** Label every container and bin in your under-sink cabinet. Even if you live alone, labels help you return items to the right place every time - which is the real secret to maintaining organization long-term. [Source: realsimple.com](https://www.realsimple.com)
## Must-Have Products for Under Sink Organization

Now that you have a solid set of under sink organization ideas, here's a quick rundown of the most helpful product types to look for. **Pull-out cabinet organizers** are the workhorses of under-sink organization. Look for U-shaped or split-level designs that straddle the center pipe. Most are adjustable in width, which is essential for different cabinet sizes.
**Clear acrylic or plastic bins** give you instant visibility into your storage and make it easy to group items by category. Look for bins with a lip or handle so you can pull them out as a unit.
**Tension rods** are inexpensive and incredibly versatile. Beyond hanging spray bottles, they can serve as dividers inside bins to keep bottles from toppling over.

**Lazy susans** come in various sizes - typically 9-inch, 11-inch, and 12-inch diameters. Choose based on your cabinet's interior dimensions. Non-slip turntables work best for preventing items from sliding off.

**Stackable shelf risers** can be bamboo, metal wire, or plastic. Metal wire options allow you to see everything at a glance and provide excellent airflow, which matters in damp spaces like under the sink.
**Door-mounted organizers** range from simple adhesive hooks to full-panel organizers with multiple pockets. Measure your door's interior panel before purchasing to ensure a proper fit.
**Cleaning caddies** are especially useful in the kitchen. Look for a caddy with a handle and multiple compartments so you can carry your cleaning essentials throughout your home.
**Moisture-absorbing liners** are an underrated addition. These non-slip, waterproof liners protect the cabinet floor from drips and spills and make cleaning much easier.

## How to Organize Under Sink Cabinets Step by Step
Once you have your products ready, here's a simple step-by-step process to put everything together.
1. **Install any permanent fixtures first.** This includes pull-out organizer tracks, door-mounted racks, or adhesive hooks. Let adhesives cure fully before loading them with weight.
2. **Place your largest items first.** The pull-out organizer, shelf riser, or any large bins go in first since they form the backbone of your layout.
3. **Accommodate the pipe.** Position your organizers around the drain pipe deliberately rather than as an afterthought. U-shaped organizers are designed for this - use them.
4. **Group and load by category.** Fill each bin or basket with one category of items. Keep the most-used items in the most accessible spots - front and center.
5. **Hang your spray bottles.** If you installed a tension rod, loop the trigger handles over the rod. This instantly frees up floor space.
6. **Fill the door organizer.** Add smaller, frequently used items to any door-mounted storage you've installed.
7. **Label everything.** Use a label maker, chalkboard labels, or printable sticker labels. Label the front of each bin, basket, or drawer.
8. **Do a final check.** Close the cabinet and open it again. Can you see and access what you need easily? Is everything secure and not at risk of falling? Make any final adjustments.

## Tips to Maintain Your Under Sink Organization Long-Term
Getting organized is the first step - staying organized is the ongoing practice. Here are some tips to keep your under-sink cabinet tidy for months and years to come.
• **Do a quick reset once a month.** Take five minutes to pull everything out, wipe down the surface, toss empty bottles, and return items to their designated spots.
• **Follow the one-in, one-out rule.** Every time you bring a new cleaning product or toiletry under the sink, an old or empty one must leave.
• **Keep a trash bag dispenser handy.** If you store trash bags under the kitchen sink, a roll dispenser mounted inside the door makes restocking effortless.
• **Check for leaks regularly.** A dripping pipe can silently ruin your organization system and damage your products. Inspect for moisture every time you do your monthly reset.
• **Buy only what fits.** It's tempting to stock up, but overstuffing defeats the purpose of organization. Keep backstock limited to what fits in its designated bin.
• **Involve everyone in the household.** If everyone knows the system - where things live and why - the cabinet is far more likely to stay organized over time.

## Under Sink Organization Ideas on a Budget
You don't need to spend a lot of money to get your under-sink cabinet in order. Some of the most effective solutions are also among the most affordable.

**Tension rods** are often available for under US$5 and may be the single highest-value purchase you can make for under-sink storage. One rod, installed in seconds, completely changes how you store spray bottles.
**Dollar store bins and baskets** can work surprisingly well for grouping items together, especially in the bathroom. Look for consistent sizes so they stack neatly.
**Repurpose what you have.** Shoeboxes covered in contact paper, old gift boxes, or mason jars can all serve as low-cost organizers for small items.
**Magnetic spice jars** repurposed on a magnetic strip can hold small bathroom items like bobby pins, safety pins, or hair ties without taking up any shelf space at all.
**Stackable recycled containers** from your pantry or garage can double as under-sink organizers for cleaning supplies, especially if they already have lids.
You can also check out [Good Housekeeping's guide to small-space organization](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com) for additional budget-conscious ideas that work in tight cabinets.

## FAQ: Frequently Asked Questions About Under Sink Organization Ideas
**Q: What is the best organizer for under the kitchen sink?**

The best organizer for under the kitchen sink is typically a two-tier pull-out cabinet organizer with a U-shape cut-out to accommodate the drain pipe. This type of organizer maximizes vertical space, allows easy access to items in the back, and keeps cleaning supplies neatly contained. Pair it with a tension rod for spray bottles and a door-mounted rack for a fully optimized setup.
**Q: How do I organize under my bathroom sink when there's very little room?**

When space is limited, think vertically. Use a stackable shelf riser or a set of small stackable drawers to create multiple levels of storage within the same footprint. A lazy susan is also very effective in tight spaces because it gives you access to items in the back without needing extra room to reach. Finally, use the inside of the cabinet door with adhesive hooks or a slim door-mounted organizer.
**Q: How do I keep cleaning supplies safe from children under the sink?**

Install a childproof cabinet lock on your under-sink cabinet doors. These are inexpensive and easy to install. Additionally, keep the most hazardous products - like drain cleaner or bleach - on higher shelves in another location entirely if possible, reserving the under-sink space for safer everyday items.
**Q: How often should I reorganize under my sink?**

A full reorganization once or twice a year is usually sufficient if you do a quick monthly reset. The monthly reset - which takes about five minutes - involves wiping down the surface, tossing empty or expired products, and returning misplaced items to their correct bin. This prevents the gradual accumulation of clutter that makes full reorganizations feel overwhelming.
**Q: What should I NOT store under the sink?**

Avoid storing anything that is sensitive to moisture or humidity, including medications, vitamins, paper documents, or electronic accessories. Also avoid storing items you use very infrequently - those belong in deeper storage elsewhere. The under-sink cabinet should be reserved for items you access regularly as part of your kitchen or bathroom routine.
**Q: What is the best way to deal with the drain pipe when organizing under the sink?**

Choose organizers specifically designed for under-sink use - they typically feature a U-shaped cutout or a split design that wraps around the pipe. For bins and baskets, simply place them to the left and right of the pipe rather than in front of it. You can also use the space directly in front of the pipe for flat items like extra sponges, cleaning wipes, or folded trash bags.
